Hi Ben / Sara —

Thanks for the context — below are concrete suggestions you can use in the POC. I'm including a draft YAML (model-routing-policy-draft.yaml) that demonstrates routing tiers, fallbacks, and a cost/latency preference example.

SDK & auth (quick notes)
- SDK: our "redwood-js" and "redwood-go" clients support region hints at call time (region_hint parameter) and automatic retries. See redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf for snippets.
- Auth: for POC we recommend scoped API keys with short TTL (rotate daily). For production, mTLS + mutual auth with certs + customer-managed KMS is supported (we have a KMS integration template in the enterprise repo).

Model routing & policy patterns
- Latency-first policy (example): route to same-region low-latency instance pools; if 95th pct > target or pool saturated, failover to secondary region with warmer cache. This keeps tail latency predictable.
- Cost-first policy: prefer cheaper quantized model variants and CPU-based endpoints for low-priority batch/async requests; route interactive chat to GPU pools.
- Fallback chain example (see attached YAML):
  primary: model-A-gpu (local-region, strict latency SLO)
  fallback: model-A-gpu (secondary-region)
  degraded-fallback: model-A-quant (local-region, lower cost, slightly higher latency)
  final-fallback: model-B-quant (cheapest)

Structured output & tool calling
- Use structured output mode for intent extraction and tool-calling hooks; SDK supports a tools API where the model response can include a canonical JSON action. We recommend a schema for external action payloads and a pre-flight validator in your app.

Embeddings & reranker patterns
- Store embeddings in your vector DB (we have an embeddings API that integrates with common vector stores). For sub-200ms rerank budgets, keep candidate set small (n <= 50) and run reranker as a short-context model; cache embeddings and use prefix caching for hot queries.

Attachments: model-routing-policy-draft.yaml (policy example + comments).

I'll be on a call Monday morning but available Tue/Wed for a 30m architecture session. Marcus can provide a capacity + cost estimate.

Cheers,

Hi team —

Following up with capacity and policy recommendations from our infra side, plus a proposed mutual action plan. Quick bullets: 

- Region routing: configure region hints (us-east-1 / us-west-2) from your app tier. For autoscaling we recommend a primary local pool sized for 2x baseline traffic with a cold standby in the secondary region to minimize failover time.
- Fallback & cost controls: enforce token/cost budgets per route and a circuit-breaker that moves traffic to quantized variants when spend threshold is crossed. The attached estimate (acme-integration-estimate.xlsx) contains two scenarios (baseline / peak).
- SLA considerations: we can commit to latency targets for Dedicated pools; hosted plans will have best-effort fallback guarantees. We'll include clear metrics for 95th pct and error budgets in the MPA.

Proposed mutual action plan:
1) Tue/Wed next week 30m architecture session (confirm a slot)
2) Redwood delivers policy YAML + cost worksheet (this week) — attached
3) Acme shares sample traffic profile + sample dataset for rerank evaluation
4) POC: 2 weeks, success criteria: 95th pct chat latency < 300ms, rerank P95 < 200ms, embedding recall threshold 0.85

Ben — if that looks good I can produce a slightly more detailed flow diagram and a DocuSign MPA for signatures.
